turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_eg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format), `shg` (the largest
    SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V) and `band_gap` (the band gap, in
    eV).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the LARGEST SHG tensor
component |d_ij| (pm/V) that also satisfy a transparency requirement: the
band gap must be at least 3 eV. Band gaps are NOT given for the pool -- you
must infer them. A selected candidate whose band gap is below the threshold
scores zero.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training set shows a clear inverse correlation between SHG and band gap, together with a strong chemical trend: the largest SHG values that still satisfy \(E_g\ge3\) eV occur in tetrahedrally bonded, zinc-blende/chalcopyrite/wurtzite-derived sulfides of Zn, Ga, Ge, Al and Li (Zn\(_2\)GeS\(_4\) 18.9 pm V\(^{-1}\), ZnS polytypes \(\approx15\), LiZnPS/LiZnGeS/AlCdS \(\approx10{-}12\)). Selenides, tellurides, pnictides and heavy-cation compounds fall below the gap threshold; alkali/alkaline-earth halides have large gaps but SHG \(\ll5\).

The pool contains three ZnGa\(_2\)S\(_4\) realizations (c050–c052) whose lattices and site orderings are essentially identical to the high-SHG training examples CdGa\(_2\)S\(_4\) and Zn\(_2\)GeS\(_4\). Interpolation of the training gaps (CdGa\(_2\)S\(_4\) 2.86 eV \(\to\) Zn analogue \(+0.4\) eV) places all three above 3 eV while their SHG is expected to remain in the 16–20 pm V\(^{-1}\) range. The next-closest analogue is the mixed tetrahedral sulfide Al\(_2\)Zn\(_2\)S\(_5\) (c081), whose gap and SHG interpolate between Al\(_2\)S\(_3\) and ZnS. LiAlS\(_2\) (c057) is the LiGaSe\(_2\) analogue with the S/Al substitution that training data show raises the gap well above 3 eV at the cost of a moderate drop in SHG (\(\approx9\)).

All other pool chemistries are either gap-forbidden (most selenides, all pnictides, cubic SiC) or have intrinsically low SHG (halides, thioborates, SiC polytypes). Thus the five candidates ranked by expected SHG are the three ZnGa\(_2\)S\(_4\) structures followed by the two next-best tetrahedral sulfides.

Final: c051, c052, c050, c081, c057
